value-case.note: Claims reconciled against code; collective leaderboard now pitched. Only the track-to-cost feature was walked end to end this run; judge/benchmark and collective were not.

monetization.note: Free and open source, no monetization. Dual MIT/Apache-2.0 is the commercial statement.

artifacts.note: 34 contexts, 213/213 file refs resolve, regenerated within a day of the run.

milestone.note: Not applicable: repo is not Personas-managed (no .personas marker).

notes.note: docs/DECISIONS.md, ADR-style D1 through D14; D14 added by this run.

fleet.note: Not applicable: repo is not Personas-managed.

cicd.note: Branch protection requires 6 checks (3 store conformance, test, clippy, fmt), all green. clippy and fmt promoted from advisory to blocking. cargo-deny stays advisory by design.

deploy.note: Deploy assets are real and every script fails loudly. No public production URL for LightTrack itself is verifiable from the repo, and no rollback has been executed once. Not raised in a decision round this run.

observability.note: Structured JSON logging to stdout, LIGHTTRACK_LOG level control, text mode for local work. 30 of 33 print sites converted.

code-quality.note: fmt clean across 240 files, clippy -D warnings clean, 723 tests pass. lt CLI split 504 LOC to 45 plus 7 modules. Deferred: store-pg/events.rs 607 LOC and api/collective.rs 1023 LOC still exceed the 300-LOC rule; one allow(too_many_arguments) in runner/bench.rs.

auth.note: Admin key and post-hash comparisons are constant-time (subtle, fixed-width digests so length never leaks). Dev mode warns loudly at boot. Still absent: rate limiting on auth-bearing routes, and an atomic key-rotate endpoint.

security.note: One advisory in 304 crates (RUSTSEC-2026-0190, unsound not vulnerability, unreachable), cleared by bumping anyhow. PII scrubbing now on by default; a relay ingest door that bypassed redaction was found and fixed. MCP writes default off. No secret in git history.

design-system.note: CLI/MCP share the render crate (verified), and the API error envelope is a genuine frozen cross-binary contract. The Grafana dashboard JSON was never verified for internal consistency.

i18n.note: English-only. No i18n framework or locale files exist; recorded as observed rather than asked, and open to the operator's correction.

onboarding.note: Documented quickstart failed silently before this run. Now: dev mode attributes a projectless event to a default project, all three SDKs warn (rate-limited, never throwing), the price book is compiled in so binary-only installs still price, and the README two-command path was run verbatim against a live instance. The judge loop still needs a separately installed claude CLI.

feedback.note: CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, two issue forms, PR template. GitHub private vulnerability reporting enabled. Community health 14 to 85 percent.

landing.note: README is the front door and now opens with a working two-command quickstart. No docs site; GitHub Pages is off.

seo.note: Repo description, homepage and 8 topics set. Cargo.toml your-org placeholder corrected.

legal.note: LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE at root, Apache text byte-identical to apache.org. GitHub detection resolves; was 404 before.

analytics.note: Product is telemetry-free, verified by grep across crates and clients. Adoption signal is GitHub counters only, currently zero.

launch-gate.note: Proven on v0.0.7, the first successful release run in repo history. docker.yml smoke-gated both arch legs pre-push (real project, minted key, ingested event, cost_usd=0.00045 from the book on amd64 and arm64); release.yml built all four platforms including the first x86_64-apple-darwin asset ever shipped, and the verify job passed. The published Windows binary was then downloaded and run from a config-less directory: cost priced, source 'compiled-in default'.

release.note: latest and v0.0.7 share digest sha256:9581c137. First release with a complete four-platform asset set since v0.0.2.

acceptedRisks: clippy is a blocking gate against a floating stable toolchain, so a future Rust release can red-wall CI with no code change. This happened once during the run (local 1.94 vs CI 1.97); the operator chose to accept it rather than pin.
No rollback has been rehearsed, and no public production URL for LightTrack itself is verifiable from the repo.
No rate limiting on auth-bearing routes.
The Python and TypeScript SDKs are still unexercised by CI; only clients/rust has a job.
